title: AI on mobile limb-lead ECG detects acute myocardial infarction in a prospective cohort
summary: A deep learning ECG model applied without retraining to mobile limb-lead ECGs reached an AUC of 0.843 (95% CI 0.758-0.928) for acute myocardial infarction in 153 patients (25 with AMI) referred for coronary angiography. At a high-sensitivity threshold its sensitivity was 88.0% versus 20.0% for cardiologists reading limb leads and 40.0% for 12-lead reading. This is a single-center prospective cohort with 25 events, a version 1 preprint abstract.
ai_technology: Deep learning AMI-detection model developed on 12-lead ECGs, applied without retraining to mobile limb-lead ECGs at two prespecified thresholds

evidence.tested: Prospective observational cohort with angiography in all patients and prespecified thresholds; comparison with three cardiologists.
evidence.unknown: Specificity trade-offs, larger multicenter performance and outcome benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Detects AMI from a short mobile recording where clinicians perform poorly.

source_review.scope: Version 1 abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations not retrieved. Full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
